messages:
sanjay: Heads-up — ACME reported they couldn't validate a RBAC change event in our audit feed last night. They have a compliance check that failed. Can someone pull the timeline?

maya: on it. which org/actor?

sanjay: org acme-inc. The customer says they saw a permission grant at 2024-11-09T22:41Z in their UI but the audit export only shows a role assignment without the requester info.

emma: I pulled a sample from our audit store for that time range. two relevant events: a role.grant and a kms.decrypt used by the rollout service. logs look like this:
```
ts=2024-11-09T22:41:12Z event=role.grant resource=org/acme-inc/role/Editor principal=principal:service/runtime-agent principal_type=service_account meta.request_id=abc123
ts=2024-11-09T22:41:13Z event=kms.decrypt key_id=kms:arn:.../redwood/keys/012345 meta.request_id=abc123 outcome=success
```

liam: that principal looks like the runtime-agent, not a human. ACME claims their admin clicked the UI to grant. Could be a UI action that proxied through runtime-agent. Need to tie request_id back to auth path.

maya: searching traces for request_id=abc123... found a proxy entry in the control-plane logs showing oauth token exchange:
```
ts=2024-11-09T22:41:11Z cp.request id=abc123 user=alice@acme-inc oauth_client=redwood-console scope=roles:grant
```

emma: so oauth user alice exchanged -> control plane invoked runtime-agent to perform grant. Our audit schema currently has fields: actor, actor_type, agent_id, request_id, and action. ACME's validator expects 'requester' and 'actor_email' fields. Looks like the schema rename in v2 (actor -> principal) might be causing mapping mismatch for customer exports.

sanjay: ugh. We shipped schema v2 mappings last week to streamline principal fields. Did we update the export-mapper used for customer CSV/JSON exports?

liam: quick check: export-mapper version shows 1.3.2 — it still maps actor->requester incorrectly for v2. I think the customer-facing export didn't include actor_email.

support-bot: support ticket #8742 created and linked to ACME; notified them we are investigating.

maya: action plan: 1) confirm full timeline to prove human initiated 2) fix export-mapper so exported audit events include requester/actor_email for backward compatibility 3) backfill customers that ran exports in the last 24h 4) add validation test to prevent regressions.

emma: for 1) I correlated CP logs + control-plane traces + audit store; timeline shows: UI click by alice -> oauth token -> cp request id abc123 -> runtime-agent grant -> kms.decrypt for key 012345 -> audit role.grant with agent principal. So we can prove alice initiated. I'll assemble a concise timeline to send to ACME.

liam: for 2) I'll open a patch: export-mapper should include legacy fields 'requester' and 'actor_email' when mapping v2 entries. Quick patch appended:
```diff
- output.actor = entry.principal
+ output.requester = entry.actor || entry.principal
+ output.actor_email = entry.actor_email || entry.principal_email
```

maya: please add a unit test that loads a v2 event and validates both legacy and v2 fields are present.

liam: will do. Also we need to consider KMS key rotation obfuscating key ids for customers. ACME said key id was different in their side-by-side. That was because our KMS proxy masks full ARNs for PII; we should include a stable key fingerprint in exports.

emma: noted. I'll add an audit field key_fingerprint = sha256(key_arn) so customers can correlate without exposing ARNs.

sanjay: good. For the immediate customer response: confirm timeline and offer to re-run their export for the period with the compatibility fields and key_fingerprint. Also offer to redact ARNs if they prefer.

support-bot: replied to ticket #8742 with "we can re-run export with compatible schema and provide timeline proving action initiated by alice@acme-inc; engineering is patching the export-mapper."

auditor-bot: flagged this thread as "audit-export-compat" and created incident link INC-2024-1109-AUDIT for postmortem.

maya: follow-ups: - PR for export-mapper patch -> review by tomorrow - backfill job for affected customers -> run once patch lands - add an automated end-to-end exporter test to CI using a fake CP trace + audit store to catch mapping regressions.

liam: PR opened: github.com/redwood/infer/export-mapper/pull/412. includes tests and key_fingerprint change.

emma: I'll draft the customer-facing timeline email and attach anonymized logs. sanjay can review.

sanjay: thanks team. after we close this, let's add a short runbook for "customer claims missing requester info" so support can triage faster. :thumbsup:

maya: noted and will add to eng-security wiki under runbooks.

liam: ETA for deploy is 6h after approval — will coordinate with eng-releases for a low-risk window.

support-bot: ticket #8742 updated: "export re-run scheduled, timeline delivered, engineering patch in review."

emma: delivering timeline now to ACME -> sending: "Attached is the correlated timeline and we confirm the action was initiated by alice@acme-inc via the console; the audit event recorded the service principal that executed the grant. We're re-running your export with compatible fields and a key fingerprint for correlation. Expected ETA 8 hours."

sanjay: great. close loop on postmortem once INC-2024-1109-AUDIT has a draft. Thanks.
